title: Adding HBr to propene
caption: Step 1: the π electrons attack the δ+ hydrogen and the H–Br bond breaks. Hydrogen adds to the end carbon, so the positive charge sits on the middle carbon: a secondary carbocation, more stable than the primary one the other way round would give. Step 2: bromide's lone pair bonds to the positive carbon. The major product is 2-bromopropane; 1-bromopropane forms only as a minor product.
alt: Mechanism of HBr adding to propene: the π bond attacks hydrogen to form a secondary carbocation and bromide, then bromide attacks the carbocation to give 2-bromopropane.
description: Left: propene and hydrogen bromide, with δ+ on hydrogen and δ− on bromine. A curly arrow goes from the C=C double bond to the hydrogen. A second curly arrow goes from the H–Br bond to bromine.

Middle: the secondary carbocation CH₃–C⁺H–CH₃ (positive charge on the middle carbon, bonded to two other carbons) and a bromide ion. A curly arrow goes from a lone pair on bromide to the positive carbon.
Right: 2-bromopropane, the major product. Hydrogen added to the end carbon and bromine to the middle carbon.

review.notes: Round 1: added H drawn as a stray –H; minor route not shown; fixed (CH3 label; caption explains the less stable primary cation). Round 2: approve.
